messages:
nina: FYI: spike in GPU attach failures in eu-central ~00:45-01:10 UTC. A mix of preemptible and a couple of dedicated nodes ejected. dmesg shows a mix of PCIe AER and nvme metadata complaints. Noticed remap_count stays 0. Anyone seen AER -> nvme metadata flips before?

nina: ```
[00:47:18] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[00:47:19] nvme0: metadata commit mismatch, seq=0x12f, expected=0x130
[00:47:19] nvme0n1: flagged bad block at LBA 0x3a2f
[00:47:20] nvme0: controller reset due to media error
[00:47:21] kernel: nvme_core: ctrl shutdown complete
```

rishi: which nodes and are they on the kernel we rolled yesterday?

nina: gn-ec-1902 (dedicated), gn-ec-1905 (preemptible), gn-ec-1911 (preemptible). All three are on kernel 6.2.14 that rolled in the morning.

marco: remap_count=0 and SMART OK suggests controller-level metadata state inconsistent (maybe due to AER-induced incomplete firmware transactions) rather than NAND failure. We saw something sort of similar last year but this time AER is prominent in the log.

ops-bot: Auto-evict: gn-ec-1905 triggered (reason: nvme.badblocks_detected). Grace window applied; attach backoff increased.

nina: I temporarily disabled aggressive janitor scrubs on eu-central and increased attach retry window to 90s. Also set instance-park policy to keep dedicated workers for critical workloads.

taylor: Can we reproduce in lab? I'll spin up a test rig (same PCIe root + firmware) and inject a synthetic PCIe correctable event while running janitor to see if nvme flags the metadata. If we can repro, vendor ticket will be easier.

marco: Action list: 1) collect nvme id-ctrl, smartctl -a, pci ids, and firmware versions from all three hosts. 2) run nvme debug dump (admin cmd 0x02) for last crashlog blob. 3) capture dmesg + perf traces around AER. I'll take the data collection.

nina: Pushed a small canary: revert kernel to 6.1.21 on one test host (gn-ec-1902-canary) to see if behavior changes. If canary is stable, we'll consider rolling back eu-central.

sre-bot: Correlation scan: 9 nodes across eu-central show pcie AER entries within the same 30m window. Upstream fabric reported a brief lane margin change at the same time (carrier telemetry). Confidence: medium-high.

rishi: Network/fabric-induced lane margin changes could cause correctable PCIe errors. If firmware or kernel treats certain AER sequences as fatal to pending admin writes, that could flip metadata. We should engage vendor with full AER traces + crashlogs.

vendor-bot: Reminder: attach logs to ticket template VENDOR-IO-2026 (include nvme crashlog, AER logs, pci topology, and firmware binary versions).

nina: Finance note: if we reserve extra capacity in eu-central to cover attach SLOs while we fix, rough estimate ~30 instances @ $400/mo each = ~$12k/mo. Tagging finance to approve short-lived buffer.

finance: Acknowledged. Please add start/end dates and we'll pre-approve a 2-week buffer for incident mitigation.

marco: Edge case: if controller firmware handles AER by marking in-flight metadata as invalid then remap_count could remain zero while upper layers see partial writes and flag blocks. Vendor confirmation needed.

taylor: Lab plan: repro steps into ticket: 1) run continuous 32MB janitor writes to test volume, 2) at t=60s inject AER correctable sequence via pci-stress tool, 3) monitor nvme crashlog and kernel for metadata mismatch. I'll try tonight.

nina: For immediate customer impact: 1) we're throttling scrubs in eu-central, 2) increasing attach backoff, 3) holding a small pool of dedicated nodes to keep critical GPU jobs flowing. I'll post updates every 30m.

rishi: If rollback needed, call it now. We have rollback playbook for kernel rollouts.

nina: Thanks — tagging @marco @taylor for lab and @vendor-bot for the ticket. If anyone needs console access to gn-ec-1902, DM me. :thumbsup:
